inputs.share_count_basis: closing shares on issue at 31-Mar-2026 (164.246m, FY2026 AR / kpis SharesOnIssueClosing) — NOT the CSV weighted average 149.553m, which understates the count because the NZ$5m raise closed January 2026. No dilutive-securities table adjustment material; count held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed (charging both would double-count).
inputs.net_debt_note: own cash 4.521 (post Jan-2026 raise), total debt 0. Customer payroll float of 45.155 held at FY2026 is EXCLUDED — it is exactly offset by 'funds due to customers and IRD' and is not the company's money. FY2019-FY2020 CSV cash figures still include the float and must not be read as company liquidity.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: OCF 1.975 (correctly float-excluded, 'before increase in funds due to customers and IRD') less capex 2.210 (predominantly capitalised software development — a cash cost an owner bears, so the owner-FCF basis already expenses it). The float-inclusive OCF headline of 9.196 (kpis OCFIncludingCustomerFloat) is NOT distributable and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash flow statement / Metrics.csv StockBasedComp; no separate net-share-settlement tax line disclosed (immaterial for an NZX filer of this size)
inputs.interest_income_note: Only interest on the company's OWN cash (~0.02 est.; the raise landed Jan-2026) is stripped from the FCF base, because that cash (4.521) is added to equity value. Float interest (~1.79 of the 1.813 total) is genuine operating revenue: its source asset (customer float) is NOT added to enterprise value, so keeping the income in the flows satisfies the matching rule. It is modelled as its own explicit, rate-dependent driver — never grown at a SaaS rate.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (two-driver variant) per dcf-methods routing — operating SaaS company. Revenue is split into (1) processing/subscription fees + other (FY2026: 7.434, +11.5% YoY) grown on scenario paths, and (2) interest income on the customer payroll float (FY2026: 1.813, -22% YoY), modelled explicitly as a rate-dependent line — the two must never share a blended growth rate. FY2017-FY2018 rows are Energy Mad Ltd (the reverse-takeover shell) and are excluded from every CAGR and multiple. FY2026 owner FCF is negative (-0.959): the company only looked profitable because 2.21 of development cost was capitalised; on a cash basis it did not cover its own dev spend in FY2026. Terminal value is tax-normalised at 28% so the 8.258 loss pool is not perpetuated. Forsyth Barr forecasts cited in the Analysis JSON are commissioned research and were used only as a cross-check on the direction of FY2027 losses, not as an anchor.

wacc_rationale.currency_basis: NZD flows discounted at an NZD-built rate: NZ 10yr govt ~4.4% + NZ equity risk premium — standard NZ small-cap cost of equity ~11.5%
wacc_rationale.notes: NZ$37m market cap, ~NZ$7k/day turnover (severe illiquidity, +2.0). Revenue ~100% NZ with an agriculture/dairy customer skew (+1.0). Founder-CEO holds 20.7% and has personally relocated to run the AU launch (+0.5). AU execution risk is primarily charged in the scenario flows and weights (bear 25%); only a residual +0.5 sits in the WACC to avoid charging the same risk twice (owner-fcf.md section 7f). ~20% of revenue is wholesale-rate-dependent rather than execution-dependent (+0.5). Zero debt, so WACC = cost of equity. Same 16% used for all three scenarios — per-scenario WACC differences would charge risk a third time.

historical_growth.history_note: PaySauce operating history starts FY2019; FY2017-FY2018 (Energy Mad shell) excluded from all CAGRs.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case year-1 processing-fee growth (FY2026 actual +11.5%, Q1 FY2027 +11% YoY, tapered): the controllable revenue line, NOT the blended figure
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs are capital-raise-driven (Jan-2026 NZ$5m raise), not retained earnings — unusable as a growth anchor. Blended revenue CAGRs are inflated by the 2022-24 rate-cycle surge in float interest (0.21 -> 2.33 FY2022-FY2025, now reversing). Owner-FCF CAGR undefined: the SBC-adjusted series is negative in most years (FY2021 -1.82, FY2022 -0.84, FY2023 -0.11, FY2024 +0.09, FY2025 -0.20, FY2026 -0.96).

base.narrative: Australia gains a modest foothold: processing-fee growth accelerates from 10% to a 13% peak as AU adds customers off the Payday Super catalyst, then decays to 5% by FY2036 (revenue NZ$19.7m). Pre-SBC EBITDA margin dips to 8% in FY2027 on AU go-to-market spend, then ramps to a mature 28%. Capitalised-development capex tapers from 22% to 10% of revenue post platform build. Float interest steps down to ~NZ$1.45m as the OCR cycle bottoms, then grows slowly with the float. Cash tax is sheltered by the NZ$8.26m loss pool through the explicit window; the terminal year is tax-normalised at the full 28%.
base.da_convention: D&A set equal to capex each year (steady-state); tax shield flows through EBIT
base.terminal_tax_normalization: terminal FCF taxed at full 28% statutory rate regardless of remaining loss pool — prevents perpetuating the tax shelter into the Gordon terminal

bull.narrative: Payday Super (1 July 2026) lands as a genuine forced-adoption catalyst and the partner channel activates: processing fees compound at 15-28% through FY2030 as AU scales (revenue NZ$40m by FY2036), margins reach 32% pre-SBC with AI-led cost-to-serve, and the AU float roughly doubles interest income by FY2036. Losses are consumed by FY2035 and the company is a full 28% taxpayer at terminal.
bull.da_convention: D&A set equal to capex each year (steady-state); tax shield flows through EBIT
bull.terminal_tax_normalization: terminal FCF taxed at full 28% statutory rate regardless of remaining loss pool — prevents perpetuating the tax shelter into the Gordon terminal

bear.narrative: Australia consumes the January-2026 raise and is wound back by FY2029: partner-channel recruitment stalls (management's own risk register flags ~60% dependence), AU pricing already ~20% below plan. NZ is simultaneously squeezed — Xero/MYOB bundling, platform-migration churn, agri downturn — holding processing growth at 2-6%. Interest income falls to NZ$1.0m as rates trough. The NZ-only business never covers its own development spend plus SBC: owner FCF stays negative until FY2035, terminal value sits near the zero floor, and the equity value is negative — a second, deeply dilutive raise would be required.
bear.da_convention: D&A set equal to capex each year (steady-state); tax shield flows through EBIT
bear.terminal_tax_normalization: terminal FCF taxed at full 28% statutory rate regardless of remaining loss pool — prevents perpetuating the tax shelter into the Gordon terminal

scenario_flags: BEAR HITS EFFECTIVE FLOOR: bear terminal FCF is barely positive (0.08 tax-normalised), terminal value 0.59 sits near the zero floor, and bear equity value is NEGATIVE (-0.75m, -$0.005/share): on that path the Jan-2026 raise is consumed and a further dilutive raise is required. The bear case says the equity does not survive the path without new money — a finding, not a rounding detail.

Base case pays zero cash tax in all 10 explicit years (8.258m loss pool + investment-phase losses); terminal year is tax-normalised at 28% to avoid perpetuating the shelter. Residual pool at FY2036 (base ~6.8m) is conservatively given no value.

entry_price.hurdle_note: HURDLE (15%) IS BELOW THE 16% WACC, so mechanically the hurdle entry price sits slightly ABOVE intrinsic value — the 15% IRR screen is not binding for this name. The operative buy-below discipline is the weighted IV itself ($0.042); the entry-price block is retained for contract compatibility.

required_return_table.note: base-scenario flows with the WACC-Gordon terminal value (tax-normalised), discounted at each required return; the 16% row equals the base IV

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because the thesis rests on an unproven pivot (AU launched April 2026, 40 customers, pricing already ~20% below plan, management's own risk register flags ~60% partner-channel dependence) and the bear path leaves negative equity value. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right simultaneously: partner-channel activation, Payday Super conversion, NZ platform migration without churn, and float interest stabilising.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position 5.2 means the price sits ~5x beyond even the street (SBC-as-non-cash) ceiling of the base case: the market is not paying for either accounting basis of the current business — it is paying for bull-case Australian success at a much lower discount rate.

sanity_check.basis_note: P/E computed on SBC-adjusted EPS both sides; only FY2024 had positive adjusted EPS, so the P/E anchor is a single observation. EBITDA basis is the company's reported EBTDA (already SBC-expensed) — SBC not deducted twice. For a company loss-making for most of its life, P/SALES AND P/B ARE THE MEANINGFUL ANCHORS; P/B is itself distorted by a near-zero (once negative) book, so P/Sales is primary. These deliberately differ from screener P/E figures which use GAAP EPS. FY2017-FY2018 shell years excluded.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.ev_ebitda_note: EBTDA only positive from FY2025; no meaningful history

sanity_check.price_position_10yr_range: 0.225 is in the LOWER half of the PaySauce-era (post Aug-2018 RTO) range 0.165-0.831
sanity_check.diagnosis: No overvaluation trip: base IV implies 0.61x sales / 0.60x book / 0.92x EBTDA — far BELOW both the historical averages and the current price's 4.0x sales. The trip tests target DCFs that out-run history; this one runs the other way. The gap is the market pricing bull-case Australian success (and, implicitly, a much lower discount rate than the 16% a micro-cap of this liquidity warrants).
sanity_check.note_on_tax_fix: One methodology fix was self-caught during the build (before the sanity gate): the first pass perpetuated the NZ$8.26m tax-loss shelter into the Gordon terminal; terminal FCF is now tax-normalised at 28%, which cut base IV from 0.042 to 0.034.

valuation_philosophy: This valuation deliberately reads as brutal against a NZ$0.225 price. PaySauce's FY2026 owner FCF is NEGATIVE (-0.96m): reported profit exists only because 2.21m of development cost was capitalised, ~20% of revenue is wholesale-rate interest on other people's money (falling as the OCR eases), and the company is entering a multi-year Australian investment phase that its own commissioned research models as loss-making through FY2028. At a 16% NZD cost of equity — justified line-by-line by micro-cap illiquidity (~NZ$7k/day turnover), sector/country concentration, key-person and residual execution risk — even a bull case in which Australia broadly works (NZ$40m revenue, 32% margins by FY2036) is worth ~NZ$0.10. The current price therefore embeds both bull-case AU execution AND a discount rate this liquidity profile does not merit. The stock is an option on Australia, and the model prices the option honestly rather than capitalising the hope.
dashboard_banner: Model approach: owner-FCF DCF with the revenue split into processing fees (grown) and float interest (rate-dependent, modelled flat-to-down — never extrapolated). Customer payroll float (NZ$45.2m) is excluded from cash; FY2017-18 shell years excluded from history; terminal value tax-normalised at 28%. The sanity check did NOT trip on overvaluation — the DCF sits far BELOW the market price: weighted IV NZ$0.042 vs NZ$0.225, because at a 16% micro-cap discount rate the market price can only be justified by bull-case Australian success. This is an option-on-Australia stock, not a cash-flow stock, at today's price.
